cards.text: Hosea, a prophet of the LORD, tells this one himself. Back when the LORD first spoke to him, Hosea married a woman named Gomer (Hosea 1:2-3). Now, friend, it's a heavy one: his wife is loved by another man, she's an adulteress, and the LORD speaks to Hosea.

cards.question: Hosea's wife is loved by another man. What does the LORD tell Hosea to do about her?

answers.text: Go show love to her again
Let her go her own way
Send her back to her family

cards.text: AGAIN? After ALL that, I'd have dropped a whole tray of cookies right there, but God tells Hosea exactly what kind of love this is.

cards.question: The LORD tells Hosea to love his wife the way the LORD loves the ___, even though they turn to other gods.

cards.text: And God says the Israelites love to offer raisin cakes to idols. Good baking, handed to an IDOL, and as a baker I'm offended on behalf of every oven I've ever met.
So Hosea goes, and he doesn't just ask her to come home. He buys her back.

cards.question: Hosea buys back his wife for fifteen shekels of ___ and some barley.

cards.text: Fifteen shekels AND barley, and Mother Miller pulled me out of a closing-sale bin for one QUARTER. Then Hosea sits his wife down and tells her how it's going to be.

cards.question: Hosea tells his wife she must live with him for many days. What must she not do?
Hosea asks this of his wife but promises nothing in return.

cards.text: Now those many days come up again, and this time they're about the Israelites.

cards.question: For many days, what will the Israelites live without?

cards.text: No king, no prince. No sacrifice or sacred pillar either.

cards.question: During those many days, Israel will still have its ephod and its idols.

cards.text: But Hosea isn't done, because after those many days comes an afterward. That's me at the end of a long bake, nose pressed to the oven door, waiting to see what comes out.

cards.question: After those many days, the people of Israel will return and seek the LORD their God.
Israel will seek the LORD their God and ___ their king.

cards.text: That's David, king over Israel long before Hosea's day (2 Samuel 5:3). And Hosea says, "They will come trembling to the LORD and to His goodness in the last days."

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards points to the Israelites rather than the Egyptians or Philistines. The baker can only recall or guess the missing name, not reason it out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Hosea bought his wife back; it gives no basis for inferring silver rather than gold or bronze. This blank tests an arbitrary detail the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Hosea asks this of his wife" does not explain what "this" means. The requirement being discussed appears only on card 9, so this question relies on a card the baker can no longer see instead of supplying its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Two answers name pairs of leaders, while "Their homes or their fields" names property. The answers are therefore not all the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No earlier card gives a clue that David, rather than Saul or Solomon, belongs in the blank. The baker must know or guess the unseen wording instead of reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
